The blood fill cue borrows from design-coded bullet lists and the modern blood-type-marker aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as blood coded rather than literal a-button-coded shape.

In real-world usage 🅰️ lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate blood-type-marker energy. A partner sends it on a 'blood 🅰️' blood-type-marker marker. A friend sends it on a 'a-pulse pulse 🅰️' reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'blood coded 🅰️' list thread. The blood fill cue is what makes the emoji feel blood coded — it is not just 'shape,' it is 'blood coded a-button moment.'
